The Data of a dbartsData Object

model.frame.dbartsData.Rd

Read the model's variables and the number of rows of a dbartsData object.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'dbartsData'
model.frame(formula, ...)
# S3 method for class 'dbartsData'
nobs(object, ...)

Arguments

formula, object

A dbartsData object.

...

Not used.

Details

model.frame returns the model's variables over the rows in, after subset and the na.action, as model.frame of an lm fit does: the response first, factors as factors, the weights in a (weights) column and the offsets in the offset() and (offset) columns, so that model.response, model.weights and model.offset read them. Its "na.action" attribute is the object's. On an object that keeps its frame it is made from the frame; where the frame holds a sparse column, which model.frame cannot read, it is the frame decoded from the block, as for an object with no frame.

On an object with no frame (a sampler's data, keep.data = FALSE, the matrix interface, an environment) it is decoded from the block where that is exact: the response is returned in its recorded type and levels (a factor, a logical, a character vector, a Surv response where the object holds its time and status, the count matrix for a multinomial one) and named as the formula wrote it (log(price), and y where no formula did), a factor predictor as a factor over its declared levels, and a matrix term such as poly(x, 2) as one matrix column again, named as the formula wrote it, with the column names the term gave. The block holds no more than the values, so a rejoined matrix has none of the attributes poly() or scale() give it (their class, coefficients and centers); every other column is as held.

nobs counts every row in, rows of weight 0 included, which a BART fit holds in its trees; nobs of an lm fit leaves them out.

Value

A data frame, and a number.
